hypothesis: Routing the shared SRAM to the NPU (clearing bit 1 of SYSCTRL 0x03000008) is needed for the finite numerical image to compute correct outputs.
prediction: With the SRAM routed to the CPU the NPU jobs complete but compute wrong outputs; with bit 1 cleared while the NPU resets are held, outputs match the reference.

The reference backsolve found that the vendor kernel powers domain 4 before any NPU clock or reset change: its NPU driver compiles out runtime power management and the platform bus attaches the device to its power domain with power-on before probe. Before the change the sequencer requested domain 4 ON after the local open table; its register pass also refused an enabled PLL_NPU, so a second NPU start in one power lifetime needed a power removal. The boot ROM uses its stack at 0x000f3400 in that SRAM; the forced-FEL return that SunstoneOS images use enters at 0x20 and zeroes 0x00044000-0x000f3ffc before it reaches 0x20c. The production sequence, the power-first order and adoption of a running PLL_NPU were tested by the three-start runbook docs/board-runbooks/npu-starts.md.

hypothesis: The routing, power-first order and register window add little startup cost and no per-job work.
conclusion: Measured in the host model of the sequencer (checks/npu-startup-host.c) and on the linked finite image; the before column is revision 37502c21. With routing and the power-first order alone, the 2 ms settle started after the PLL LOCK wait inside a tick, which cost one tick once per startup; the event-driven settle end removes it. The register window costs one acquire load and one compare per register access, at most a few hundred per job. No digest, translation, copy, queue round trip or cache operation is added (section 3 of the performance architecture).
narrative: Boot to READY, domain 4 OFF at entry: 11 ticks, 11,000 us, 12 calls before; 12,001 us, 13 calls after with routing and the power-first order alone; 4,628 us, 4 calls with the startup latency changes (docs/designs/npu-board-measurements.md, startup latency change by change). Register reads besides LOCK samples, writes, lock acquisitions: 57, 12, 3 before; 61, 13, 4 after. Local stop reads, writes: 12, 5 before; 15, 6 after. Second start with PLL_NPU and domain 4 adopted: refused, power removal before; 4,414 us, 6 writes, 3 LOCK samples, no PLL, gate-control or PCK600 write after. Instructions from the convolution backend's register read to the adapter call: 33 before, 39 after (one an acquire load). EL3 return: one to three SYSCTRL accesses. Finite default image functions, .text: 139,564 and 148,520 bytes before; 140,512 and 150,568 bytes after.

conclusion: Both 37502c21 and the change were built from clean archives, extracted in turn at one tree path and built in turn into one build path (every default central target, the NPU board image, the convolution model, the supervised, resident and NPU-profile OS images, the accelerator composition, the finite image in four profiles).
